parsed.explanation: The combined regime carries universal, state-imposed exposure at the national document and entry layer: passports are restricted to sex-at-birth markers, X-marker issuance has stopped, passports have been confiscated or blocked leaving some travellers stranded, and discrepancies trigger refusal and a possible lifetime fraud finding. Documented custody harm (immigration-custody forced labour and sexual abuse; corrections care denial) and a documented criminal-trespass arrest for facility use, held 24 hours, sit on top of this. The division adds a school-only bathroom restriction with no documented statewide adult rule, a minors' care ban, a birth-certificate surgery requirement, a hate-crime statute that omits gender identity, and a 2018 appellate employment protection. Remedies are partial and litigation is unresolved. No death penalty or likely imprisonment is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports restricted to M/F by birth sex; X markers no longer issued; discrepancies lead to refusal and requests for more evidence; possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; athlete-entry ban; documented passport confiscation and blocking leaving travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; a civil-liberties suit is pending; the Supreme Court allowed restrictions to take effect, so no operative protection is documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry flows into refusal, extra questioning, and possible permanent ineligibility; national rules override any division-level protection.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Facility-trespass arrests in 4 states, one documented (handcuffed, held 24 hours in men's ward).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Pretrial release was granted in the documented arrest; no documented custody protocol for trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A bathroom-trespass stop can convert to custody and placement by birth sex, linking facility rules to custody harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans cover all government buildings in 10 state/provinces, schools and some government buildings in 9 more, schools-only in 3; 6 extend to some private settings. The division's school bathroom restriction applies to public school students only; no statewide adult rule is documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 state/provinces, 4 others and the capital district have no mapped ban; the division has no adult facility rule documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National and division rules run in parallel; a visitor in a ban state faces exposure in government buildings regardless of the division's narrower scope.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for minors with no phase-out; national proposed rules would bar public insurance for under-18s; national subpoenas sought records of under-19 patients; national youth crisis services were shut down.
care_services.protection: No division-wide adult care restriction is documented; the minors' care ban has remained in force through appellate review.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking minors may be exposed to record subpoenas and reporting; adult care access is not documented as restricted at division level.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as a priority for neutralisation; a reward scheme targets leadership linked to the same category; executive orders direct investigation of schools and criminal prosecution of teachers for facilitating social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing of trans advocacy as security threat raises discovery and scrutiny risk for travellers linked to activism.

minors_guardians.exposure: School facility restriction for minors; minors' care ban with no phase-out; sport closure; national threat of prosecution for teachers and schools; record subpoenas for under-19 patients; a travelling minor may face passport mismatch and possible entry refusal.
minors_guardians.protection: Some federal orders are blocked; the division's school rule is applied via district guidance that urges caution on bathrooms.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian with a minor faces school-linked exposure, care-record exposure and document-based refusal in combination.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division hate-crime statute excludes gender identity; 37 states lacked gender-identity bias statutes as of 2019; no division trans-specific violence statistics; the one documented division case was a sexual-orientation prosecution.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 22 states plus DC bar gender-identity discrimination; 19 municipalities have local ordinances covering gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse for a visitor depends on location: the national statute and municipal ordinances help, while the division's hate-crime gap leaves most bias violence outside enhancement.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport refusals have no documented effective remedy; facility and care rules are in litigation with outcomes unresolved; the appellate status of the 2023 care ban and the 2013 religious-service statute are unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Ombuds-style complaints exist; some federal orders have been enjoined; municipal ordinances and the 2018 appellate employment holding operate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists in the courts but is slow and uneven, so exposures persist between rulings.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: both have state-imposed, traveller-facing entry exclusion with weak remedy. This case is somewhat higher because it has no exclusion register and passports are not all refused. It is lower because it adds documented custody sexual abuse and forced labour, which the 0.35-A anchor lacks.

Similar: both document birth-sex custody harm, assaults and weak remedies. This case is somewhat higher because the division's adult rules are narrower, there is no documented capital or imprisonment pathway, and national hate-crime and municipal protections operate in places.

Similar in universal-exposure weight through document checks. This case is somewhat lower because it adds documented custody abuse and criminal facility arrests, and the anchor has no documented custody harm.

parsed.synthesis: The dominant traveller exposure is the national document regime: sex-at-birth passports, refusals on discrepancy, possible lifetime ineligibility, and documented stranding. This feeds into custody, where immigration detention has produced documented forced labour and sexual abuse, and facility-trespass arrests show that bathroom use can become custody. Facility bans reach government buildings across many states, though the division's own rule is school-only and adult-facing rules are not documented there. Minors face the heaviest combined exposure from care bans, school rules, record subpoenas and threatened prosecution. Protections such as the national hate-crime statute, municipal ordinances and the 2018 employment holding operate in parts, but remedies are slow and partial. No death penalty or likely imprisonment is documented, so the rating sits in the elevated band.
